name: Aegis Edge
tagline: Air-gapped defence for embedded devices: detects sensor tampering and has a local LLM write and flash a firmware patch.
problem: Hospitals, bases and plants cannot send sensor data to the cloud, so tampering on the wire goes unseen.
solution: A Python bridge reads ventilator-rig telemetry, detects anomalies from a Flipper Zero attack, asks a local 70B model to write a virtual-sensor patch in Arduino C++ and reflashes the board over USB.
demo_moment: Team-described: red-team attack on the ventilator rig, then the automatic patch and recovery.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Attack and defence happen live on hardware in the room.

lessons: Stage the attack live; a recovery is only convincing after a visible failure.
